turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that his wife must not worry about the future, that the family's prosperity would be ensured, and that he would care for their son and daughter-in-law.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid nervously asked if the tea was to be served now, glancing at O-lan with concern for her mother-in-law's well-being.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was tired of hearing him speak of the family's prosperity, and that she wished to see it for herself before she died.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he was willing to listen to her wishes and would do everything to make her happy before she passed away.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan's eyes narrowed as she gazed at Wang Lung, her voice low and even as she told him not to try to ease her mind with words, for she had seen the look in his eyes and knew he was worried.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he could see the exhaustion in her eyes and that she must not think of the future, for he was there to care for her and their son.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he would work harder to bring honor to the family and make her proud, and that he would soon be married and start his own life, just as she wanted.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung to take the eldest son to the city to look for a bride, for she wanted to see her son wed and settled before she died

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would take the eldest son to the city immediately, but only if O-lan would promise to rest and not worry about the future, for her own health was all that mattered to him.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: She told Wang Lung that she knew his words were meant to comfort her, but she must see her son wed and settled before she could die in peace.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he could not bear the thought of her dying, and that he would rather die himself than live without her.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that the eldest son must be wedded to the maid, and that she wanted to see the ceremony take place before she passed on, as it would bring her peace of mind.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan must not worry about the wedding, for it could wait until her health improved.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told O-lan and Wang Lung that he would be honored to marry the maid and bring peace of mind to his mother, and that he was willing to go to the city immediately to make the arrangements.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: She is pleased that her son has agreed to marry the maid, and she wants him to know that she will not rest until the wedding is planned and underway.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: He insisted that O-lan must rest and not exhaust herself with such thoughts, for her health was the only thing that truly mattered to him.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told the eldest son that she would make sure the wedding preparations began immediately, and that the maid would help her with the arrangements.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: the eldest son assured O-lan that he would make sure the wedding was simple and modest, so as not to put a strain on her health

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told the eldest son that she would need the maid to help her with the wedding preparations, and that she wanted the youngest son to be present at the ceremony, but only if his health permits it.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: the eldest son assured O-lan that he would make sure the youngest son's health is taken care of, and that the family will be there to support him through the wedding preparations and beyond

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
